title: Symb-xMIL: Symbolic Explanations for Multiple Instance Learning in Digital Pathology
claim: A multi-stage procedure converts a black-box model's behavior on input subsets into a rule-based symbolic representation supporting both local and global explanation.
layout: 5 numbered stages left-to-right, two rows, A/B output panels, bottom legend
description: A wide, dense pipeline diagram with five numbered blue headers running left to right: input and preprocessing, semantic features/queries/subsets, model evaluation, similarity to logical queries, and the symbolic representation space. On the left a histology slide image becomes a patch grid with colored squares for semantic labels. Colored circles stand for concepts and are combined into 1st-, 2nd- and 3rd-order subsets, then into logical queries using AND, OR and NOT. A neural-network icon labeled MIL model feeds a blue bar chart of subset responses. A purple bar chart gives the query-induced reference vector. A correlation box links the two and produces a table of alignment scores per query, with a red-blue colorbar. At the far right, two framed panels show (A) local best-aligned-query explanation and (B) global clustering scatter. A dashed legend strip runs along the bottom.
caption: Overview of the Symb-xMIL pipeline. Patches from a WSI are assigned semantic labels and grouped into a feature set of concepts (1–2). Multi-order subsets and a query space of logical rules are constructed over these concepts (2). The MIL model is evaluated on each subset, and the resulting subset responses are compared against query-induced reference patterns (3–4). The resulting alignment scores form the symbolic representation ϕ(X), in which each dimension corresponds to one logical rule (5). This representation supports (A) local explanation through the best-aligned query for a single sample, and (B) global analysis through clustering across samples.
abstract: Explanations of multiple instance learning (MIL) models are widely used for validation and discovery in digital histopathology. Existing methods primarily rely on heatmaps that highlight influential regions but do not explain how evidence from different tissue regions is combined to produce a prediction. This limits interpretability, especially when decisions depend on interactions between tissue features. We introduce Symbolic explainable MIL (Symb-xMIL), a post-hoc explanation framework that quantifies how a MIL model's behavior aligns with human-readable decision rules, expressed as logical relationships (e.g., AND, OR, NOT) between input features. These alignment scores reveal semantic patterns underlying the model's predictions. We evaluate Symb-xMIL on synthetic and real-world histopathology datasets. On synthetic MIL data, Symb-xMIL reliably recovers ground-truth logical rules. In a clinical tumor detection task, the best-aligned rules uncover heterogeneous decision patterns and expose hidden model errors. On an HPV-prediction task on TCGA-HNSCC, a cohort of head and neck cancer, our framework refines patient survival stratification beyond HPV status with potential clinical relevance. Overall, Symb-xMIL extends MIL explainability beyond visual attribution toward structured, rule-based reasoning, enabling more transparent and semantically grounded interpretation of model predictions.
